Now `TestCompiledFunctionCallNestedTransferIsolation` fails because the map closure now returns 152 instead of 151. Why? Because with recursive binding, the array and map closures now share the same bound copy! So calling `incArr` (n 0→1, returns 151), then calling `incMap` (same shared n, 1→2, returns 152). That's actually MORE correct — it preserves sharing within the transferred composite value!
